provenance.primary-source: packages/core/src/dropdown/{Dropdown.tsx,Dropdown.css} for the trigger; packages/core/src/option/{Option.tsx,Option.css,OptionList.tsx,OptionList.css,OptionListBase.tsx,OptionGroup.tsx,OptionGroup.css} for the popup and its contents; packages/core/src/list-control/ListControlState.ts (via Dropdown.tsx) for the selection/typeahead model. Dropdown composes these — they are separate exported components shared with ComboBox and ListBox, which is why docs/SELECT-MATRIX.md's scope note flags every popup/option row as a migration candidate if `option`/`popover` are later split out.
provenance.accent-pin: Salt's editable-borderColor-hover/-active and every selectable-* stop resolve through palette-accent*, which carries a data-accent axis (blue default, teal alternate — next/palette/accent.css). This column pins BLUE, Salt's default, the same scope trim button.salt.json and input.salt.json made; only calendar.salt.json models byAccent so far.
provenance.field-bg / field-bg-secondary / field-bg: Dropdown.css .saltDropdown-{primary,secondary,tertiary} { --dropdown-background: var(--salt-editable-{variant}-background) } -> next/characteristics/editable.css -> palette-background-{primary,secondary,tertiary} -> snow 255,255,255 / marble 245,247,248 / limestone 250,248,242 light; jet 16,24,32 / granite 26,34,41 / leather 38,41,43 dark. Identical resolution to input.salt.json, cross-checked rather than re-derived.
provenance.field-bg-readonly: --dropdown-background-readonly -> editable-background-readonly -> --salt-color-transparent. All three variant blocks set it, so a read-only Salt dropdown is transparent at every variant.
provenance.fg / fg-disabled: --dropdown-color -> content-primary-foreground (declared identically in all three variant blocks and in all three status blocks); .saltDropdown:disabled { color: var(--salt-content-primary-foreground-disabled) } -> black-40a / white-40a
provenance.fg-secondary: ONE token, TWO consumers: .saltDropdown-placeholder { color: var(--salt-content-secondary-foreground) } and .saltOptionGroup-label { color: var(--salt-content-secondary-foreground) } -> palette-foreground-secondary -> gray-700 (76,81,87) light / gray-300 (177,181,185) dark. The placeholder additionally sets font-weight: var(--salt-text-fontWeight-small) -> typography fontWeight-light = 300.
provenance.border / border-hover / border-active: --dropdown-borderColor -> editable-borderColor -> palette-neutral -> gray-500 (114,119,125), identical in both mode blocks; -hover -> editable-borderColor-hover -> palette-accent -> blue-500 (0,120,207), also mode-invariant; -active -> editable-borderColor-active -> palette-accent-stronger -> blue-700 (0,69,126) light / blue-300 (154,189,245) dark. --dropdown-outlineColor -> focused-outlineColor, which is the same palette-accent-stronger stop, hence outline-current aliases border-active.
provenance.border-readonly / border-disabled: Dropdown.css hangs these off the ATTRIBUTE [aria-readonly="true"] and the :disabled pseudo-class respectively (not classes) -> editable-borderColor-readonly -> palette-neutral-readonly -> gray-500-10a; editable-borderColor-disabled -> palette-neutral-disabled -> gray-500-40a. Both mode-invariant.
provenance.accent / accent-weakest / accent-weaker: next/characteristics/selectable.css: --salt-selectable-borderColor-selected -> palette-accent (blue-500, mode-invariant) — used BOTH as OptionList's border and as the selected option's bracket; --salt-selectable-background-hover -> palette-accent-weakest -> blue-100 (234,246,255) light / blue-900 (0,23,54) dark; --salt-selectable-background-selected -> palette-accent-weaker -> blue-200 (199,222,255) light / blue-800 (0,45,89) dark. --salt-selectable-background itself is color-transparent.
provenance.status-*: Dropdown.css .saltDropdown-{error,warning,success} { --dropdown-borderColor: var(--salt-status-{s}-borderColor) } -> next/characteristics/status.css -> palette-{negative,warning,positive} -> red-500 229,33,53 / orange-500 199,83,0 / green-500 0,135,93, all mode-invariant. Matches alert.salt.json and input.salt.json exactly.
provenance.status-*-bg: --dropdown-background / --dropdown-background-readonly -> status-{s}-background -> palette-{role}-weakest -> the 100 stop light / 900 stop dark.
provenance.popup-bg: OptionList.css .saltOptionList { background: var(--salt-container-primary-background) } -> next/characteristics/container.css -> palette-background-primary -> snow / jet. The same surface value as a primary-variant trigger, arrived at through the CONTAINER characteristic rather than the EDITABLE one.
provenance.popup-shadow: OptionList.css box-shadow: var(--salt-overlayable-shadow-popout) -> next/characteristics/overlayable.css -> --salt-shadow-mediumLow. Value reused from docs/foundations/elevation.md (0 6px 10px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.2) light / 0.55 dark) rather than re-derived, the same reuse tooltip.salt.json made.
provenance.separator-color: OptionGroup.css .saltOptionGroup { border-top: var(--salt-size-fixed-100) solid var(--salt-separable-tertiary-borderColor) } -> next/characteristics/separable.css -> palette-alpha-contrast-mediumLow -> black-20a light / white-20a dark (foundations/alpha.css).
provenance.popup-gap: OptionList.css .saltOptionList-container { gap: var(--salt-spacing-fixed-100) } = 1px. The FIXED spacing scale is density-invariant by design (foundations/spacing.css declares --salt-spacing-fixed-100: 1px once, outside every density block), so this literal is not a frozen snapshot of a scaling token — the TOOLTIP-MATRIX.md check was run and passed.
provenance.popup-min-width: Dropdown.tsx's floating-ui size() middleware writes elements.floating.style --overlay-minWidth = `${rects.reference.width}px`, and OptionList.css reads it as min-width. This column aliases a slot whose value is var(--select-trigger-width), an inline custom property skeleton/select.tsx measures and sets on the popup — the same inline mechanism, minus the positioning engine (declared gap).
provenance.byDensity.control-height: Dropdown.css min-height: var(--salt-size-base) -> foundations/size.css 20/28/36/44px. NOTE it is min-height, not height, unlike Input.css which sets both.
provenance.byDensity.field-padding: Dropdown.css padding: 0 var(--salt-spacing-100) — literally zero vertical padding, min-height alone sets the rhythm. spacing-100 = 4/8/12/16px.
provenance.byDensity.field-gap: THREE source declarations, one token: .saltDropdown-startAdornmentContainer { margin-right: var(--salt-spacing-100) }, .saltDropdown .saltDropdown-toggle { margin-left: var(--salt-spacing-100) }, and StatusAdornment.css's own padding-left. Modelled as a single column-gap — a declared, visually equivalent simplification.
provenance.byDensity.corner-weak / popup-corner: Dropdown.css border-radius: var(--salt-palette-corner-weak, 0) -> curve-100 = 2/4/6/8px; OptionList.css border-radius: var(--salt-palette-corner, 0) -> curve-150 = 3/6/9/12px. Two DIFFERENT corner stops on the same component — the popup is deliberately rounder than the control. Rounded edition pin, same as button/tooltip/input (docs/foundations/shape.md).
provenance.byDensity.type-body: Dropdown.css font-family/-size/-weight/-line-height/letter-spacing -> --salt-text-* body role. Unlike Input.css, Dropdown.css DOES declare font-weight explicitly (var(--salt-text-fontWeight) -> typography fontWeight-regular = 400), so the 400 in this shorthand is sourced rather than ambient. Option.css declares the identical five properties, which is why style.option.font aliases the same slot.
provenance.byDensity.type-group-label: OptionGroup.css .saltOptionGroup-label uses the LABEL role: --salt-text-label-fontSize/-lineHeight (10/13 · 11/14 · 12/16 · 14/18 by density, next/characteristics/text.css density blocks) with --salt-text-label-fontWeight-strong -> typography fontWeight-semiBold = 600.
provenance.byDensity.toggle-icon-size: DECLARED COMPOSITION. Dropdown.css sizes nothing on .saltDropdown-toggle except margin-left; the box comes from the composed icon component — packages/icons/src/icon/Icon.css: --icon-size: max(calc(var(--salt-size-icon) * 1), 12px). size-icon is 10/12/14/16 by density, so the CLAMPED result is 12/12/14/16. The 12px floor is Salt's own documented minimum ('Icons should never be smaller than 12px for readability'), i.e. the high-density value is a real clamp, not the frozen-token case TOOLTIP-MATRIX.md warned about — checked in both directions.
provenance.byDensity.adornment-size: StatusAdornment.css height/min-height: var(--salt-size-adornment) = 6/8/10/12px. Already a density token in source.
provenance.byDensity.option-min-height / option-pad: Option.css min-height: calc(var(--salt-size-base) + var(--salt-spacing-100)) = 24/36/48/60; padding: calc(var(--salt-spacing-100) + var(--salt-spacing-25)) var(--salt-spacing-100), with spacing-25 = 0.25 * spacing-100, giving 5/4 · 10/8 · 15/12 · 20/16. Internally consistent: 10 + 16 (medium body line-height) + 10 = 36. OptionGroup.css's label repeats both formulas verbatim.
provenance.byDensity.popup-max-height: PARTIAL, declared. Dropdown.tsx writes --overlay-maxHeight = max(calc((var(--salt-size-base) + var(--salt-spacing-100)) * 5), calc(<availableHeight>px - var(--salt-spacing-100))). Only the five-row floor is expressible without the positioning engine: 5 * (20+4)=120, 5 * (28+8)=180, 5 * (36+12)=240, 5 * (44+16)=300.
provenance.border-width-literals: 1px = --salt-size-fixed-100, 2px = --salt-size-fixed-200 (foundations/size.css). Density-INVARIANT by design (docs/foundations/sizes.md), so kept as literals deliberately.
provenance.min-width-literal: Dropdown.css min-width: 4em — a bare literal with no override variable at all (Input.css at least offers --saltInput-minWidth). em-relative, so it already tracks the density-driven font size.
provenance.focus-outline: Dropdown.css .saltDropdown:focus { outline: var(--salt-focused-outlineWidth) var(--salt-focused-outlineStyle) var(--dropdown-outlineColor) } -> focused.css: 2px, dotted (foundations/borderStyle.css), accent-stronger — reassigned to the status colour by the .saltDropdown-{status} blocks. Option.css uses the shortcut token --salt-focused-outline for the same three values, with outline-offset: calc(var(--salt-size-fixed-100) * -2) = -2px.
provenance.cursors: foundations/cursor.css: --salt-cursor-hover: pointer (used by BOTH .saltDropdown:hover/:focus and .saltOption), --salt-cursor-disabled: not-allowed, --salt-cursor-readonly: text. Note the trigger cursor is POINTER here, where Salt's Input uses `text` — a button, not a text field.
provenance.no-shadow-no-motion-on-trigger: Dropdown.css contains no box-shadow, no transition and no animation rule anywhere; OptionList.css has a box-shadow but likewise no motion. Confirmed absences by full-file read.
provenance.form-field-context: Dropdown.tsx useFormFieldProps(): disabled = Boolean(disabledProp) || formFieldDisabled; readOnly = Boolean(readOnlyProp) || formFieldReadOnly; validationStatus = formFieldValidationStatus ?? validationStatusProp; required = formFieldRequired ? ['required','asterisk'].includes(formFieldRequired) : requiredProp. The necessity channel is Dropdown-only — Input.tsx does not read it.
provenance.aria: trigger: role="combobox", type="button", aria-expanded, aria-activedescendant, aria-controls (only while open), aria-readonly (only when readOnly), aria-required. Popup: role="listbox" on the FloatingComponent, aria-multiselectable when multiselect. Option: role="option", aria-selected, aria-disabled, tabIndex={-1}.

structure.indicator.note: ordered with the real default first. Dropdown.tsx: `bordered = false`, and Dropdown.css renders .saltDropdown-activationIndicator unconditionally — so an out-of-the-box Salt dropdown is an UNDERLINE, exactly as its Input is.
structure.indicator.source: Dropdown.tsx bordered?: boolean, default false; Dropdown.css .saltDropdown-bordered vs .saltDropdown-activationIndicator

structure.start-adornment.source: Dropdown.tsx startAdornment prop -> .saltDropdown-startAdornmentContainer. NOTE there is no endAdornment prop on Dropdown, unlike Input.

structure.toggle-icon.source: Dropdown.tsx ExpandIcon({open}) returns useIcon().CollapseIcon when open and useIcon().ExpandIcon when closed — two different glyphs; and the whole icon is omitted when readOnly ({!readOnly && <ExpandIcon .../>})

structure.option-group.source: packages/core/src/option/OptionGroup.tsx — role="group", aria-labelledby to an aria-hidden label div

structure.separator.note: Salt has no separator component in the option package. The same visual job is done by a border-top on the OptionGroup itself — a different mechanism, recorded as style.group.border-top rather than as a missing part.

structure.selected-marker.source: Option.tsx renders CheckboxIcon ONLY when multiselect (out of scope); a single-select Salt option is marked by Option.css's [aria-selected="true"] background + box-shadow bracket, with no glyph at all

structure.popup-anchor.source: Dropdown.tsx useFloatingUI({ placement: "bottom-start", middleware: [offset(1), size({...}), flip({fallbackStrategy:"initialPlacement"})] }) — 1px below the trigger, left edges aligned

behavior.pointer-activates-option.source: Option.tsx handleMouseOver -> setActive(optionValue); Dropdown.tsx handleListMouseOver -> setFocusVisibleState(false), so a pointer makes the option active but suppresses the focus-visible outline

behavior.status-inheritance.source: Dropdown.tsx useFormFieldProps() — see the form-field-context provenance entry, including the necessity channel Input does not read

behavior.empty-readonly-marker.source: Dropdown.tsx emptyReadOnlyMarker = "—"; valueText = readOnly && displayedValue === "" ? emptyReadOnlyMarker : displayedValue

behavior.readonly-suppresses-popup.source: Dropdown.tsx handleOpenChange early-returns on readOnly; handleKeyDown early-returns on readOnly; {!readOnly && <ExpandIcon/>}; OptionList open={... && !readOnly && ...}; aria-readonly="true" on the button

behavior.multiselect.note: DECLARED OUT OF SCOPE — recorded as a real Salt capability, not modelled. `multiselect` switches the selection model to an array, joins the trigger value with ", ", sets aria-multiselectable, renders a CheckboxIcon in every Option and changes Tab's commit behaviour.

prop.size.note: no size prop — trigger height is --salt-size-base, i.e. the DENSITY capability rather than a per-instance prop. The nearest thing to shadcn's size axis is the density toggle.

prop.validation-status.note: FormFieldValidationStatus = Omit<ValidationStatuses,'info'> — info is deliberately excluded, the same enum Input takes.

prop.disabled.source: Dropdown.tsx disabled prop, OR-ed with form-field context; written onto the <button> as the native disabled attribute

prop.read-only.source: Dropdown.tsx readOnly prop, OR-ed with form-field context; expressed as aria-readonly because a <button> has no native readonly

style.trigger.background@box.note: `bordered` declares a border and nothing else (Dropdown.css .saltDropdown-bordered.saltDropdown) — the background is untouched. A confirmed non-variation.

style.trigger.width.source: Dropdown.css .saltDropdown { width: 100% } — a Salt dropdown fills its container

style.trigger.min-width.source: Dropdown.css min-width: 4em — a bare literal, not even behind an override variable

style.trigger.shape@box.note: corner radius is independent of `bordered` — one border-radius declaration on .saltDropdown serves both

style.trigger.cursor.source: Dropdown.css .saltDropdown:hover and .saltDropdown:focus { cursor: var(--salt-cursor-hover) } -> foundations/cursor.css: pointer

style.trigger.shadow.note: no box-shadow anywhere in Dropdown.css — a confirmed absence

style.trigger.transition.note: no transition and no animation rule anywhere in Dropdown.css

style.indicator.border@underline.source: Dropdown.css .saltDropdown-activationIndicator { border-bottom: var(--salt-size-fixed-100) var(--salt-borderStyle-solid) var(--dropdown-borderColor) } — the SAME indirection the box border reads

style.trigger.background@hover.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — Dropdown.css's only :hover declarations are the cursor, the border colour and the indicator colour. The background never changes on hover.

style.trigger.border@box-focus.source: Dropdown.css .saltDropdown-bordered.saltDropdown:focus { border-color: var(--dropdown-borderColor-active) } — recolour only, width unchanged

style.indicator.border@box-focus.source: Dropdown.css zeroes the indicator under .saltDropdown-bordered, EXCEPT .saltDropdown-bordered.saltDropdown:focus .saltDropdown-activationIndicator { border-bottom-width: var(--salt-size-fixed-100) } — source comment: 'Activation indicator width minus the border from the input.'

style.trigger.focus.source: Dropdown.css .saltDropdown:focus { outline: var(--salt-focused-outlineWidth) var(--salt-focused-outlineStyle) var(--dropdown-outlineColor) } -> 2px dotted accent-stronger, or the status colour

style.trigger.background@box-disabled.note: Salt's disabled background is indicator-independent — one rule covers both

style.value.placeholder.note: DECLARED RENDERING APPROXIMATION, identical to input.salt.json's: weight 300 (fontWeight-light) is source-true but this repo self-hosts Open Sans at 400/600 only, so the browser resolves 300 to the 400 face. The sourced value is kept.

style.toggle-icon.size.source: packages/icons/src/icon/Icon.css --icon-size: max(calc(var(--salt-size-icon) * var(--icon-size-multiplier)), 12px) with multiplier 1 -> 12/12/14/16 by density
style.toggle-icon.size.note: DECLARED COMPOSITION — the glyph belongs to a future icon component. Dropdown.css sizes nothing on .saltDropdown-toggle.

style.toggle-icon.color.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — .saltIcon's fill is currentColor and Dropdown never applies .saltIcon-primary/-secondary, so the chevron inherits the trigger's own colour (including its disabled 40%-alpha value)

style.adornment.size.note: [R] as a registry choice: .saltDropdown-startAdornmentContainer declares only margin-right, so whatever it holds sizes itself. Aliased to the same composed-icon box the toggle uses, which is what a Salt icon adornment resolves to in practice.

style.status-adornment.color.note: aliased to the border indirection because in source they resolve to the identical value: --statusAdornment-color -> status-{s}-foreground-decorative -> palette-{role}, and --dropdown-borderColor -> status-{s}-borderColor -> the same palette-{role}

style.popup.color.note: declared on .saltOption rather than on the list in source (Option.css color: var(--salt-content-primary-foreground)); modelled on the popup with the option inheriting, which renders identically

style.popup.border.note: the ACCENT colour, not a neutral — the same token the selected option's bracket uses, so the list frame and the selection frame are literally one value

style.popup.shape.source: OptionList.css border-radius: var(--salt-palette-corner, 0) -> curve-150 — a ROUNDER stop than the trigger's corner-weak

style.popup.padding.source: OptionList.css .saltOptionList-container declares display/flex-direction/gap/max-height/min-height and NO padding — options run edge to edge inside the accent frame. (Contrast .saltListBox, the standalone component, which does add 1px top/bottom.)

style.popup.min-width.source: OptionList.css min-width: var(--overlay-minWidth), written inline by floating-ui's size() middleware as the trigger's own width
style.popup.min-width.note: Resolves the trigger width DIRECTLY on the popup, not through a second slot. Fixed in validation: the first build declared `--popup-min-width: var(--select-trigger-width, 0px)` at theme scope and aliased to it, but a var() inside a custom-property declaration is substituted at the element that DECLARES it - the theme root, where the skeleton's inline --select-trigger-width does not exist - so it computed to the 0px fallback and inherited down as 0px. The popup rendered 190px narrower than its own trigger. The slot now carries only the 0px DEFAULT; the skeleton's inline declaration on the popup overrides it, and the min-width rule reads the property on the element where it is actually set.

style.popup.max-height.note: PARTIAL — only the five-row floor of Dropdown.tsx's max(...) is expressible; the availableHeight half needs the positioning engine this skeleton declares as a gap

style.popup.animation.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — no animation or transition rule in OptionList.css or Dropdown.css; the list appears instantly, the same total absence TOOLTIP-MATRIX.md found on Salt's tooltip

style.option.color.source: Option.css color: var(--salt-content-primary-foreground) — Salt is the only system that declares a colour on the option itself

style.option.font.source: Option.css declares the same five --salt-text-* body properties the trigger does — an option reads exactly like the value it will become

style.option.gap.source: Option.css gap: var(--salt-spacing-100) — the same token as the trigger's gap

style.option.shape.note: Option.css declares no border-radius; a Salt option runs flush to the popup's inner edge

style.option.active.source: Option.css .saltOption-active { background: var(--salt-selectable-background-hover) } — the IDENTICAL value as the hover rule, through a different selector; two rows because they are two rules in source

style.option.focus-visible.note: a distinct THIRD option state on top of active — set only when focusVisibleState && active (i.e. after keyboard navigation) and cleared by any mouseover. No other system has it.

style.option.disabled.source: Option.css .saltOption[aria-disabled="true"] { color: var(--salt-content-primary-foreground); background: var(--salt-selectable-background); opacity: 0.4; cursor: var(--salt-cursor-disabled) }
style.option.disabled.note: the colour and background are RESTATED in source, not merely faded — that is how Salt stops its own hover/active rules winning on a disabled option

style.option.selected.source: Option.css .saltOption[aria-selected="true"] { z-index: var(--salt-zIndex-default); background: var(--salt-selectable-background-selected); box-shadow: calc(var(--salt-size-fixed-100) * -2) 0 0 0 var(--salt-selectable-background-hover), calc(var(--salt-size-fixed-100) * -1) 0 0 var(--salt-size-fixed-100) var(--salt-selectable-borderColor-selected), 0 calc(var(--salt-size-fixed-100) * -1) 0 var(--salt-selectable-borderColor-selected) }
style.option.selected.note: reproduced layer for layer with the calc()s resolved (size-fixed-100 = 1px, density-invariant). z-index 1 (--salt-zIndex-default) lets the bracket paint over the 1px gaps between neighbouring options.

style.selected-marker.box.note: no marker element in single-select — see structure.selected-marker

style.group-label.font.source: OptionGroup.css .saltOptionGroup-label uses the LABEL typescale at --salt-text-label-fontWeight-strong (semiBold 600)

style.group-label.color.source: OptionGroup.css color: var(--salt-content-secondary-foreground) — the same token the placeholder uses

style.group-label.padding.source: OptionGroup.css repeats Option.css's padding and min-height formulas verbatim, so a Salt group label occupies a full row in the list's rhythm

style.group-label.background.source: OptionGroup.css background: var(--salt-container-primary-background) — the same value the list already has, but declared, and load-bearing: an opaque label stops a neighbouring selected option's box-shadow bracket bleeding under it

style.group.border-top.source: OptionGroup.css .saltOptionGroup { border-top: var(--salt-size-fixed-100) var(--salt-borderStyle-solid) var(--salt-separable-tertiary-borderColor) } with .saltOptionGroup:first-of-type { border-top: 0 } — reproduced with an adjacent-sibling selector

style.trigger.status@error.source: Dropdown.css .saltDropdown-error reassigns --dropdown-color, --dropdown-background, --dropdown-background-readonly, --dropdown-borderColor, --dropdown-borderColor-active and --dropdown-borderColor-hover in one block; --dropdown-color is unchanged from the variant blocks so it needs no entry here
